If the valid screens count is exactly one, the valid batteries count is exactly one, and the valid cameras count is exactly two, the phone assembly is valid. Return true if valid, false otherwise. Example: screen alpha, battery beta, camera gamma, camera gamma returns true.

title: Optical Character Recognition Fixer
spec: Post-process arrays of scanned characters using `correct(text)`. The input is an array of character string and confidence level string pairs. If the character is exactly the number zero and the previous character was exactly the letter H, change the zero to the letter O. If the character is exactly the number one and the confidence is exactly low, change it to the letter l. If the character is exactly the exclamation mark and the confidence is exactly low, change it to the letter i. If the character is exactly the dollar sign and the confidence is exactly high, leave it as a dollar sign, but if the confidence is exactly low, change it to the letter S. Return the corrected characters joined into a single string. Example: an array with H high and zero low returns H O.

title: Three Dimensional Printer Command Parser
spec: Process commands for a printer machine using `print(commands)`. Commands are provided as arrays containing an instruction, a numerical value, and a mode string. If the instruction is move x and the mode is exactly absolute, set the x coordinate to the value. If the instruction is move x and the mode is exactly relative, add the value to the x coordinate. If the instruction is extrude and the mode is exactly absolute, set the extrusion amount to the value. If the instruction is home x and the mode is exactly all, set the x coordinate to exactly zero. If the instruction is bed temp and the value is exactly zero, set a heater boolean to false. Return an array containing the final x, y, z coordinates and the extrusion value. Example: move x ten absolute returns ten for the x coordinate.

title: Carousel Ride Controller
spec: Manage the sequence of an amusement carousel with `run(controls)`. Controls are arrays containing a control name and an operator key string. The ride starts in the stopped state. If the control name is bell and the operator key is exactly valid and the state is exactly stopped, the state becomes boarding. If the control name is start and the operator key is exactly valid and the state is exactly boarding, the state becomes spinning. If the control name is music on and the operator key is exactly master and the state is exactly spinning, the state becomes lively. If the control name is stop and the operator key is exactly valid, the state immediately becomes decelerating. Return the final state. Example: bell valid, start valid returns spinning.

title: Factory Conveyor Sorter
spec: Implement a function `sort(items)` that processes a list of material strings. Track the item counts for four bins and a compost pile. Iterate through the items. If an item type is not a string, ignore it. If the item is plastic and bin one has fewer than ten items, add it to bin one. If the item is glass and bin two is open (meaning bin two has fewer than ten items), add to bin two. If the item is metal, add to bin three. If the item is paper, add to bin four. If organic, add to compost. If hazardous, return the array of counts immediately. If unknown, skip it. If empty, stop processing and return the counts. Example: sorting plastic, glass, and organic returns an array where bin one has one, bin two has one, and compost has one.

title: Coffee Roaster Profiler
spec: Write a function `roast(events)` that processes a list of arrays, where each array contains an event string and a temperature number. Track a running temperature and a boolean indicating if the roaster is running, initially false. For each event, if the event is start and the roaster is not running, set running to true. If the event is heat and running is true, add the temperature number to the running temperature. If the event is cool and the running temperature is positive, subtract the temperature number. If the event is check and the running temperature is above one hundred, do nothing. If the event is hold, keep the temperature the same. If the event is drop, return the current temperature immediately. If the event is error, return a negative one. If the event is stop, set running to false. Return the final temperature. Example: start, then heat by fifty, then drop returns fifty.

title: Hovercraft Navigation System
spec: Create a function `navigate(commands)` that tracks coordinates x, y, and z, starting at zero, and a flying boolean initially false. Iterate through the list of command strings. If the command is start, set flying to true. If up and flying is true, increase z by one. If down and z is greater than zero, decrease z by one. If left and flying is true, decrease x by one. If right and flying is true, increase x by one. If forward, increase y by one. If backward, decrease y by one. If hover, do nothing. If land, set flying to false and z to zero. Return the final x, y, and z coordinates as an array. Example: start, up, forward, right returns an array of one, one, one.

title: Orchard Irrigation Controller
spec: Develop a function `irrigate(sensors)` that accepts a list of sensor reading strings. Track the total water used, starting at zero, and an active boolean, initially true. If the sensor is dry and active is true, add ten to water used. If moist and active is true, add two to water used. If wet, add zero. If raining, set active to false. If empty, add zero to water used but increase a warning counter. If disconnected, ignore the sensor. If offline, reset active to true. If error, return the total water used so far. After processing all sensors, return an array containing the total water used and the warning count. Example: dry, moist, raining, dry returns twelve for water and zero for warnings.

title: Custom Paint Color Blender
spec: Write a function `mix(colors)` that calculates the total cost of a paint mixture. The input is a list of arrays containing a color string and a parts number. Iterate through the list. If the type of the parts value is not a number, skip that array. If the color is red and parts are greater than zero, add five per part to the cost. If blue, add six per part. If yellow, add four per part. If white, add one per part. If black, add two per part. If cyan, add seven per part. If magenta, add eight per part. If clear, add zero per part. Return the total cost as a number. Example: an array with red and two parts, plus blue and one part, returns sixteen.

title: Animal Shelter Diet Planner
spec: Create a function `feed(animals)` that calculates the daily food cost. The input is a list of arrays, each with a species string and a weight number. If the weight is less than or equal to zero, skip the animal. If the species is dog and the weight is over ten, add twenty to the total cost. If the species is cat, add ten to the cost. If rabbit, add five. If guinea, add three. If hamster, add one. If parrot, add two. If snake, add six. If turtle, add four. Return the total food cost as a number. Example: dog weighing fifteen and cat weighing five returns thirty.

title: Space Station Air Lock
spec: Implement a function `pressurize(sequence)` that processes a list of action strings. Track a pressure level starting at zero, and a locked boolean starting at false. If the action is seal and not locked, set locked to true. If the action is pump and locked is true, increase pressure by ten. If the action is vent and locked is true, decrease pressure by ten. If the action is unseal and pressure is exactly zero, set locked to false. If the action is override, set locked to false and pressure to zero. If the action is test, do nothing. If the action is abort, return negative one immediately. If the action is lock, set locked to true regardless of the current state. Return the final pressure. Example: seal, pump, pump, vent returns ten.

title: Commercial Dough Kneader
spec: Write a function `knead(ingredients)` to calculate total mixing time. The input is a list of arrays, each containing an ingredient string and an amount number. Track total time starting at zero, and a wet mixture boolean starting at false. If the ingredient is water, set wet mixture to true and add two minutes. If milk, set wet mixture to true and add three minutes. If flour and wet mixture is true, add five minutes. If yeast and wet mixture is true, add four minutes. If salt, add one minute. If sugar, add one minute. If butter, add six minutes. If egg, add two minutes. Return the total mixing time. Example: water and flour returns seven minutes.

title: Recycling Center Sorter
spec: Develop a function `recycle(waste)` that categorizes a list of waste strings into four bins. Track the counts for metals, paper, plastics, and glass, as well as a main capacity starting at one hundred. If the waste is aluminum and capacity is above zero, add one to metals. If steel, add one to metals. If cardboard, add one to paper. If newspaper, add one to paper. If pet, add one to plastics. If hdpe, add one to plastics. If glass, add one to glass. If ceramic, reduce the main capacity by one. Return an array of the four counts in order: metals, paper, plastics, and glass. Example: aluminum, cardboard, glass, pet returns one for each category.

title: Microscope Stage Motor
spec: Create a function `focus(commands)` that tracks three coordinates x, y, and z starting at zero, and a locked boolean starting at false. Iterate through the command strings. If the command is lock, set locked to true. If unlock, set locked to false. If the command is raise and not locked, increase z by one. If lower and not locked, decrease z by one. If left and not locked, decrease x by one. If right and not locked, increase x by one. If forward and not locked, increase y by one. If backward and not locked, decrease y by one. Return the final coordinates as an array of three numbers. Example: raise, forward, lock, right returns zero, one, one because the right command was blocked.

title: Aquarium Water Quality
spec: Implement a function `monitor(readings)` to calculate a severity score. The input is a list of arrays, each with a parameter string and a value number. Track a total score starting at zero and an alarm boolean starting at false. If the parameter is ammonia and the value is above zero, add ten to the score and set the alarm to true. If nitrite and value above zero, add ten. If nitrate and value above twenty, add five. If ph and value below seven, add two. If salinity and value below thirty, add three. If temperature and value above eighty, add four. If oxygen and value below five, add eight. If calcium and value below four hundred, add one. Return an array with the final score and the alarm boolean. Example: ammonia at one and ph at eight returns ten and true.

title: Wine Cellar Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(events)` that processes event strings to maintain climate. Track temperature starting at sixty, humidity starting at fifty, and a power on boolean starting at false. If the event is power, toggle the power on boolean. If cooling and power is on, lower temperature by two. If heating and power is on, raise temperature by two. If humidify and power is on, raise humidity by five. If dehumidify and power is on, lower humidity by five. If fan and power is on, keep numbers the same. If defrost, raise temperature by one regardless of power. If sanitize, lower humidity by one regardless of power. Return an array of temperature and humidity. Example: power, cooling, cooling returns fifty six and fifty.

title: Arcade Crane Game
spec: Create a function `play(inputs)` that tracks x, y, and z coordinates starting at zero, and a holding boolean starting at false. Process a list of input strings. If the input is drop and not holding, increase z by ten. If grab and z is ten, set holding to true. If up and z is greater than zero, decrease z by ten. If down and z is less than ten, increase z by ten. If left and z is zero, decrease x by one. If right and z is zero, increase x by one. If release and holding is true, set holding to false. If return, set both x and y to zero immediately. Return the final x, y, and z coordinates as an array. Example: right, drop, grab, up returns one, zero, zero.

title: Embroidery Machine Plotter
spec: Develop a function `embroider(pattern)` that processes a list of stitch strings. Track thread used starting at zero and a needle down boolean starting at true. If the stitch is straight and needle is down, add one to thread used. If zigzag and needle is down, add two. If satin and needle is down, add three. If running, add one. If chain, add two. If cross, add two. If feather, add four. If french, add five. If the stitch is stop, set needle down to false. If any valid stitch is encountered while needle is down is false, return the total thread used so far. Return the final thread used. Example: straight, zigzag, stop, cross returns three.

title: Bus Fare Collection Box
spec: Write a function `issue(coins)` that processes a list of arrays containing a coin string and a count number. Track total cents starting at zero and a jammed boolean starting at false. If the coin is penny and not jammed, add one cent per count. If nickel, add five cents per count. If dime, add ten cents per count. If quarter, add twenty five cents per count. If half, add fifty cents per count. If dollar, add one hundred cents per count. If token, add two hundred cents per count. If foreign, set jammed to true and ignore the count. Return the total cents. Example: quarter and two count, plus dime and one count returns sixty.

title: Roller Coaster Dispatcher
spec: Implement a function `dispatch(cars)` to count passengers. Process a list of car strings. Track total passengers starting at zero and an open boolean starting at false. If the car is test, set open to true. If disabled, set open to false. If standard and open is true, add four passengers. If front and open is true, add two. If rear and open is true, add two. If vip and open is true, add two. If empty, add zero. If maintenance, add zero. Return the total passengers dispatched. Example: test, front, standard, disabled, standard returns six.

title: Robot Vacuum Cleaner
spec: Create a function `clean(actions)` that processes a list of action strings. Track dirt collected starting at zero, battery starting at one hundred, and a stuck boolean starting at false. If the action is north and not stuck, decrease battery by one. If south and not stuck, decrease battery by one. If east and not stuck, decrease battery by one. If west and not stuck, decrease battery by one. If spin, decrease battery by two. If vacuum and not stuck, add two to dirt and decrease battery by three. If mop and not stuck, add one to dirt and decrease battery by four. If charge, reset battery to one hundred and stuck to false. Return an array of dirt and remaining battery. Example: north, vacuum, charge returns two and one hundred.

title: Jukebox Song Selector
spec: Develop a function `play(buttons)` to calculate total playback time. Process a list of button strings. Track total duration starting at zero and a premium mode boolean starting at true. If the button is rock and premium is true, add five minutes. If pop, add four minutes. If jazz, add six minutes. If blues, add five minutes. If country, add four minutes. If classical, add ten minutes. If metal, add six minutes. If disco, add seven minutes. If the button is skip, set premium mode to false. If any genre button is pressed and premium is false, add zero. Return total duration. Example: rock, pop, skip, jazz returns nine.

title: Slot Machine Payout
spec: Write a function `spin(reels)` that evaluates a list of spin outcomes. Each outcome is an array of three strings. Track the total payout starting at zero. For each outcome, if the first string is cherry and the second is cherry and the third is cherry, add ten to the payout. If all three are bell, add twenty. If all three are lemon, add five. If all three are orange, add five. If all three are plum, add five. If all three are bar, add fifty. If all three are seven, add one hundred. If all three are diamond, add two hundred. Return the total payout. Example: an array containing cherry, cherry, cherry returns ten.

title: Dishwasher Cycle Manager
spec: Create a function `wash(stages)` that computes a cleanliness score based on a list of stage strings. Track the score starting at zero and a door closed boolean starting at true. If the stage is prewash and door closed is true, add two to the score. If main and door closed is true, add five. If rinse and door closed is true, add three. If sanitize and door closed is true, add four. If dry, add one regardless of the door. If cool, add zero. If drain, add zero. If pause, set door closed to false. Return the final cleanliness score. Example: prewash, main, pause, rinse returns eight.

title: Train Track Switcher
spec: Implement a function `route(trains)` that processes a list of destination strings. Track the number of switches used starting at zero, and a track clear boolean starting at true. If the destination is north and track clear is true, add one to switches. If south and clear is true, add two. If east and clear is true, add one. If west and clear is true, add three. If depot, add zero switches. If siding, set track clear to false. If yard, set track clear to true. If express, add zero switches. Return the total number of switches used. Example: north, siding, south, yard, east returns two.

title: Weather Balloon Tracker
spec: Develop a function `track(data)` that processes event strings. Track altitude starting at zero and a flying boolean starting at false. If the event is launch, set flying to true. If ascend and flying is true, add one thousand to altitude. If burst and flying is true, halve the altitude. If descend and flying is true, subtract five hundred from altitude. If parachute and flying is true, subtract one hundred. If land, set flying to false and altitude to zero. If recover, return the current altitude immediately. If lost, return negative one immediately. Return the final altitude. Example: launch, ascend, descend, recover returns five hundred.

title: Stadium Entrance Turnstile
spec: Write a function `admit(tickets)` to calculate revenue from a list of ticket strings. Track total revenue starting at zero and a vip gate open boolean starting at true. If the ticket is vip and vip gate open is true, add fifty to revenue. If general, add thirty. If student, add twenty. If child, add ten. If senior, add fifteen. If staff, add zero. If press, add zero. If fake, close the vip gate by setting the boolean to false. Return total revenue. Example: general, fake, vip, student returns fifty because the vip ticket was processed after the fake ticket closed the gate.

title: Fireworks Show Sequencer
spec: Create a function `ignite(cues)` that calculates the ounces of gunpowder needed from a list of cue strings. Track the gunpowder used starting at zero and a night time boolean starting at true. If the cue is peony and night time is true, add two ounces. If chrysanthemum and night time is true, add three ounces. If willow and night time is true, add four ounces. If horsetail and night time is true, add two ounces. If crossette and night time is true, add three ounces. If ring and night time is true, add one ounce. If salute and night time is true, add five ounces. If mine and night time is true, add six ounces. If day, set night time to false. Return the total gunpowder used. Example: peony, willow, day, chrysanthemum returns six.

title: Scuba Dive Logger
spec: Implement a function `log(profiles)` to calculate bottom time. The input is a list of event strings. Track bottom time starting at zero and an in water boolean starting at false. If the event is descent, set in water to true. If bottom and in water is true, add thirty minutes to bottom time. If ascent and in water is true, add ten minutes. If safety and in water is true, add three minutes. If surface, set in water to false. If deep and in water is true, add five minutes. If deco and in water is true, add fifteen minutes. If emergency, return the current bottom time immediately. Return the final bottom time. Example: descent, bottom, surface, deco returns thirty.

title: Drawbridge Operator Log
spec: Write a function `operate(vessels)` that takes a list of lists, where each inner list represents a passing vessel's type, the river tide, and the signal used. Track bridge wear and traffic delay, both starting at zero. If the vessel type is barge, check if the signal is horn to add ten to wear. If the river tide is high, check if the vessel type is sailboat to add twenty to delay. If the signal is radio, check if the vessel type is exactly military to add five to wear. If the vessel type is not kayak, check if the river tide is low to add fifteen to delay. If the signal is flare, check if the river tide is not low to subtract five from delay. If the vessel type is exactly ferry, check if the signal is silence to add fifty to wear. Return a list containing the total bridge wear and traffic delay. Example: for [["barge", "low", "horn"], ["sailboat", "high", "radio"], ["military", "low", "radio"]], the output should be [15, 50].

title: Snowplow Router
spec: Implement `route(requests)` that accepts a list of requests, where each request is a list containing the road class, snow depth, and current plow status. Track total fuel used and roads cleared, starting at zero. If the plow status is broken, skip the rest of the rules for this request. If the road class is highway, check if snow depth is greater than ten to add three to fuel used and increment roads cleared. If the road class is street, check if the plow status is idle to add one to fuel used. If the road class is alley, check if the plow status is active to add two to fuel used and increment roads cleared. If the road class is not highway, check if the snow depth is exactly zero to subtract one from fuel used. If the plow status is refuel, add five to fuel used. Return a list with total fuel used and roads cleared. Example: for [["highway", 12, "active"], ["alley", 5, "active"], ["street", 0, "idle"]], the output should be [5, 2].

title: Beekeeping Monitor
spec: Create `inspect(hives)` which processes a list of lists representing a hive's role, its bee count, and the current season. Keep a running total of honey yield and warning flags, both initially zero. If the season is winter, check if the role is not dormant to add one to warning flags. If the season is spring, check if the role is swarming to subtract ten from honey yield and add one to warning flags. If the role is foraging, check if the bee count is greater than one hundred to add fifty to honey yield. If the role is nursing, check if the season is summer to add twenty to honey yield. If the role is guard, check if the bee count is exactly zero to add five to warning flags. If the season is autumn, check if the role is foraging to add thirty to honey yield. Return a list with the honey yield and warning flags. Example: for [["foraging", 150, "spring"], ["dormant", 0, "winter"], ["swarming", 50, "spring"]], the output should be [40, 1].

title: Ghost Hunting Equipment
spec: Design a function `investigate(readings)` that takes a list of lists, each containing a tool used, a recorded value, and the room investigated. Maintain an evidence score and a danger level, both starting at zero. If the tool is thermometer, check if the value is exactly zero to add two to evidence. If the room is basement, check if the tool is emf to add three to evidence. If the tool is spiritbox, check if the value is demon to add five to danger. If the room is attic, check if the tool is camera to add four to evidence. If the tool is not thermometer, check if the danger is exactly five to add one to evidence. If the room is not basement, check if the tool is emf to add one to danger. Return a list with the final evidence score and danger level. Example: for [["emf", 5, "basement"], ["spiritbox", "demon", "hall"], ["camera", "orb", "attic"]], the output should be [9, 5].

title: Diving Bell Operations
spec: Write `dive(logs)` to process a list of lists, where each entry contains a system name, its status, and the current depth. Track oxygen level starting at one hundred and safety status starting as true. If the system is comms, check if the status is offline to set safety to false. If the system is valve, check if the depth is greater than fifty to subtract ten from oxygen. If the system is hatch, check if the depth is not zero to set safety to false. If the system is oxygen, check if the status is venting to subtract five from oxygen. If the system is ballast, check if the depth is exactly one hundred to set safety to true. If the system is not comms, check if the status is failed to subtract twenty from oxygen. Return a list with the oxygen level and safety status. Example: for [["valve", "open", 60], ["comms", "offline", 60], ["ballast", "filling", 100]], the output should be [90, true].

title: Clockmaker Repair Tracker
spec: Develop a function `repair(clocks)` that takes a list of lists, each describing a clock part, its condition, and the maker. Track total repair cost starting at zero. If the part is pendulum, check if the condition is bent to add fifty to cost. If the maker is swiss, check if the condition is missing to add one hundred to cost. If the part is spring, check if the condition is snapped to add thirty to cost. If the maker is not swiss, check if the condition is rusted to add twenty to cost. If the part is face, check if the condition is scratched to add ten to cost. If the part is hands, check if the condition is not perfect to add five to cost. If the maker is unknown, check if the condition is destroyed to add two hundred to cost. Return a list containing only the total repair cost. Example: for [["pendulum", "bent", "german"], ["gear", "missing", "swiss"], ["face", "scratched", "unknown"]], the output should be [160].

title: Bookbinding Press Operator
spec: Implement `bind(batches)` to evaluate a list of lists representing the cover type, glue state, and stitching method of book batches. Track durability and batch time, both starting at zero. If the cover type is leather, check if the glue state is hot to add twenty to durability. If the stitching is thread, check if the cover type is cloth to add ten to durability. If the glue state is cold, check if the stitching is exactly none to subtract fifteen from durability. If the cover type is not paper, check if the glue state is tacky to add five to time. If the stitching is wire, check if the glue state is dry to add ten to time. If the cover type is exactly vellum, check if the stitching is not thread to subtract five from durability. Return a list with total durability and batch time. Example: for [["leather", "hot", "thread"], ["cloth", "tacky", "thread"], ["paper", "cold", "none"]], the output should be [15, 5].

title: Parachute Rigging Checker
spec: Create a function `pack(steps)` that processes a list of lists, each containing a parachute component, an action performed, and the inspector's level. Maintain a safety score starting at zero and a completion status starting as false. If the component is canopy, check if the action is folded to add ten to score. If the component is lines, check if the action is tangled to subtract twenty from score. If the inspector is chief, check if the component is reserve to add fifteen to score. If the action is sealed, check if the component is container to set completion to true. If the inspector is novice, check if the action is skipped to subtract thirty from score. If the component is not harness, check if the action is damaged to subtract fifty from score. If the component is slider, check if the action is exactly missing to set completion to false. Return a list with the safety score and completion status. Example: for [["canopy", "folded", "chief"], ["reserve", "checked", "chief"], ["container", "sealed", "novice"]], the output should be [25, true].

title: Volcano Observatory Alerts
spec: Write `monitor(seismic)` to assess a list of lists detailing event type, magnitude, and sensor location. Track the threat level starting at zero and an evacuation status starting as false. If the event type is harmonic, check if the sensor is crater to add five to threat. If the magnitude is exactly nine, check if the event type is explosion to set evacuation to true. If the sensor is flank, check if the event type is not tremor to add two to threat. If the event type is gas, check if the sensor is vent to add three to threat. If the event type is fracture, check if the magnitude is greater than four to add ten to threat. If the sensor is not vent, check if the event type is ash to add four to threat. After checking the rules, if the accumulated threat is exactly fifty, set evacuation to true. Return a list with the threat level and evacuation status. Example: for [["harmonic", 3, "crater"], ["explosion", 9, "vent"], ["ash", 2, "flank"]], the output should be [11, true].

title: Lighthouse Keeper Log
spec: Design `log(entries)` to parse a list of lists, where each entry has the equipment name, its current state, and the weather condition. Track fuel consumed starting at zero and a visibility warning boolean starting at false. If the weather is fog, check if the equipment is horn to add ten to fuel. If the equipment is lamp, check if the state is rotating to add five to fuel. If the weather is storm, check if the state is broken to set warning to true. If the equipment is generator, check if the state is offline to subtract five from fuel. If the weather is clear, check if the equipment is not horn to add one to fuel. If the state is jammed, check if the weather is not clear to set warning to true. Finally, if the weather is exactly hurricane, set warning to true regardless of other checks. Return a list with fuel consumed and the warning status. Example: for [["horn", "active", "fog"], ["lamp", "rotating", "clear"], ["generator", "offline", "clear"]], the output should be [12, false].

title: Pottery Kiln Controller
spec: Implement `fire(stages)` which takes a list of lists representing the firing phase, target temperature, and vent position. Track total time starting at zero and crack risk starting as false. If the phase is drying, check if the vent is open to add ten to time. If the phase is bisque, check if the temperature is exactly one thousand to add twenty to time. If the phase is glaze, check if the vent is closed to add fifteen to time. If the phase is cooling, check if the vent is not open to set risk to true. If the phase is preheat, check if the vent is open to add five to time. If the phase is not cooling, check if the vent is jammed to set risk to true. Return a list containing total time and crack risk. Example: for [["drying", 100, "open"], ["bisque", 1000, "closed"], ["glaze", 1200, "closed"]], the output should be [45, false].

title: Origami Folding Simulator
spec: Create a function `fold(instructions)` that evaluates a list of lists, each containing a crease type, folding direction, and layer count. Track thickness and aesthetic score, both starting at zero. If the crease is valley, check if the direction is inward to add five to score. If the crease is mountain, check if the direction is outward to add ten to score. If the crease is squash, check if the layer is double to add twenty to score. If the direction is reverse, check if the crease is not valley to subtract two from score. If the layer is single, check if the crease is petal to add three to thickness. If the layer is not single, check if the direction is inward to add one to thickness. If the crease is exactly crimp, add five to thickness and subtract one from score. Return a list with the final thickness and score. Example: for [["valley", "inward", "single"], ["squash", "down", "double"], ["petal", "up", "single"]], the output should be [3, 25].

title: Blacksmith Forge Bellows
spec: Write `smelt(actions)` to process a list of lists detailing the metal worked, the heat color, and the bellows speed. Keep a running tally of metal purity and carbon content, both starting at zero. If the metal is iron, check if the color is cherry to add ten to purity. If the metal is steel, check if the bellows is fast to add twenty to purity. If the color is orange, check if the bellows is stopped to subtract ten from purity. If the metal is bronze, check if the color is not yellow to subtract five from purity. If the bellows is fast, check if the metal is not steel to add two to carbon. If the color is exactly black, immediately set purity to zero and carbon to zero. If the bellows is medium, check if the metal is iron to add five to purity. Return a list with purity and carbon. Example: for [["iron", "cherry", "slow"], ["steel", "white", "fast"], ["bronze", "orange", "stopped"]], the output should be [15, 0].

title: Falconry Flight Tracker
spec: Design `track(movements)` which takes a list of lists, each recording a bird state, the flight altitude, and the prey targeted. Maintain bird energy starting at one hundred and success points starting at zero. If the bird state is perched, check if the prey is none to add ten to energy. If the bird state is hunting, check if the prey is rabbit to subtract fifteen from energy. If the bird state is diving, check if the altitude is exactly zero to add thirty to success. If the bird state is returning, check if the prey is not none to add ten to success. If the prey is pigeon, check if the bird state is not perched to subtract ten from energy. If the bird state is soaring, check if the altitude is greater than one hundred to subtract two from energy. Return a list with energy and success points. Example: for [["perched", 50, "none"], ["hunting", 100, "rabbit"], ["diving", 0, "mouse"]], the output should be [95, 30].

title: Ice Resurfacer Operations
spec: Implement `resurface(laps)` to assess a list of lists representing a resurfacer action, the tank water level, and the blade condition. Track ice quality and water used, both starting at zero. If the action is scraping, check if the blade is sharp to add ten to quality. If the action is washing, check if the water level is high to add fifteen to quality. If the action is flooding, check if the blade is not sharp to add five to quality. If the action is dumping, check if the water level is exactly zero to subtract five from quality. If the blade is dull, check if the action is not dumping to subtract ten from quality. If the action is idling, check if the water level is low to add one to water used. Return a list containing ice quality and water used. Example: for [["scraping", "low", "sharp"], ["washing", "high", "sharp"], ["dumping", "zero", "dull"]], the output should be [20, 0].

title: Truffle Hunting Dog Trainer
spec: Create a function `train(sessions)` that processes a list of lists, each describing the dog's behavior, the ground type, and the given reward. Keep track of obedience score and truffles found, both initially zero. If the behavior is sniffing, check if the ground type is soil to add two to obedience. If the behavior is digging, check if the reward is treat to add five to obedience. If the behavior is ignoring, check if the ground type is roots to subtract ten from obedience. If the behavior is alerting, check if the reward is not treat to subtract five from obedience. If the ground type is mud, check if the behavior is not digging to add one to obedience. If the behavior is eating, check if the reward is exactly none to subtract twenty from obedience. Return a list with obedience and truffles found. Example: for [["sniffing", "soil", "praise"], ["digging", "roots", "treat"], ["alerting", "mud", "none"]], the output should be [3, 0].

title: Cave Exploration Logger
spec: Write `explore(segments)` to read a list of lists, where each inner list has the caver's stance, headlamp light level, and environmental hazard. Track depth reached and battery used, both starting at zero. If the stance is walking, check if the light is high to add twenty to depth and five to battery. If the stance is crawling, check if the hazard is rocks to add five to depth and two to battery. If the stance is squeezing, check if the hazard is not water to add two to depth. If the light is low, check if the stance is rappelling to add fifty to depth and ten to battery. If the hazard is exactly pit, check if the light is off to subtract ten from depth. If the stance is not walking, check if the light is high to add three to battery. Return a list with the total depth reached and battery used. Example: for [["walking", "high", "none"], ["crawling", "low", "rocks"], ["rappelling", "low", "water"]], the output should be [75, 17].

title: Gondola Lift Operator
spec: Design `operate(cycles)` to evaluate a list of lists representing the cabin state, passenger count, and weather conditions. Track revenue and safety incidents, both initially zero. If the cabin state is loading, check if the weather is clear to add ten times the passenger count to revenue. If the cabin state is ascending, check if the weather is wind to add one to incidents. If the cabin state is maintenance, check if the passenger count is exactly zero to add nothing to revenue. If the weather is snow, check if the cabin state is not maintenance to add two to incidents. If the cabin state is emergency, check if the weather is ice to subtract fifty from revenue. If the cabin state is descending, check if the weather is not clear to add one to incidents. Finally, if the weather is exactly hurricane, set incidents to one hundred regardless. Return a list with revenue and incidents. Example: for [["loading", 5, "clear"], ["ascending", 5, "wind"], ["emergency", 5, "ice"]], the output should be [0, 1].

title: Bonsai Tree Care
spec: Implement `tend(actions)` that processes a list of lists, each detailing a care technique, the current season, and the tool used. Maintain tree health and aesthetic value, both starting at zero. If the technique is pruning, check if the season is spring to add ten to aesthetic. If the technique is wiring, check if the tool is copper to add fifteen to aesthetic. If the season is winter, check if the technique is not dormant to subtract twenty from health. If the technique is watering, check if the tool is can to add ten to health. If the technique is repotting, check if the season is exactly summer to subtract fifteen from health. If the tool is shears, check if the technique is not pruning to subtract five from aesthetic. Return a list containing tree health and aesthetic value. Example: for [["pruning", "spring", "shears"], ["wiring", "fall", "copper"], ["watering", "summer", "can"]], the output should be [10, 25].

title: Violin Maker Wood Tester
spec: Create a function `inspect(samples)` that evaluates a list of lists, where each entry represents a wood type, its acoustic resonance, and the grain pattern. Track quality score and drying time, both starting at zero. If the wood type is maple, check if the grain is straight to add ten to score. If the wood type is spruce, check if the resonance is high to add twenty to score. If the grain is curly, check if the wood type is not pine to add five to time. If the resonance is dull, check if the wood type is cedar to subtract ten from score. If the wood type is exactly plywood, check if the grain is mixed to set score to zero. If the resonance is not high, check if the grain is wavy to add fifteen to time. Return a list with the final quality score and drying time. Example: for [["maple", "high", "straight"], ["spruce", "high", "curly"], ["plywood", "dull", "mixed"]], the output should be [0, 5].

title: Hot Air Balloon Pilot
spec: Write `fly(maneuvers)` to iterate over a list of lists, each containing the burner state, wind condition, and envelope status. Maintain altitude starting at zero and fuel remaining starting at one hundred. If the burner state is blast, check if the wind is calm to add fifty to altitude. If the burner state is pilot, check if the envelope is inflated to add ten to altitude. If the burner state is venting, check if the wind is gusty to subtract thirty from altitude. If the envelope is deflated, check if the burner state is not off to subtract twenty from fuel. If the wind is exactly gale, check if the burner state is blast to subtract fifty from altitude. If the wind is not calm, check if the burner state is pilot to subtract five from fuel. Return a list with altitude and fuel remaining. Example: for [["blast", "calm", "inflated"], ["pilot", "breeze", "inflated"], ["venting", "gusty", "inflated"]], the output should be [30, 95].

title: Escape Room Reset Checklist
spec: Design `reset(props)` to process a list of lists, where each inner list contains a puzzle type, its current status, and the room location. Keep a tally of reset time and missing items, both starting at zero. If the puzzle type is padlock, check if the status is locked to add two to time. If the puzzle type is cipher, check if the status is unsolved to add five to time. If the location is desk, check if the status is exactly missing to add one to missing items. If the puzzle type is magnetic, check if the location is not wall to add fifteen to time. If the status is broken, check if the puzzle type is laser to add three to missing items. If the puzzle type is not padlock, check if the status is unlocked to add twenty to time. Return a list containing reset time and missing items. Example: for [["padlock", "locked", "door"], ["cipher", "unsolved", "desk"], ["laser", "broken", "wall"]], the output should be [7, 3].

title: Mining Drill Operator
spec: Implement `drill(operations)` to handle a list of lists detailing the drill bit state, the rock type encountered, and the coolant status. Track ore extracted and heat level, both initially zero. If the bit state is boring, check if the rock type is soft to add twenty to ore. If the bit state is extracting, check if the coolant is active to add fifty to ore. If the bit state is jammed, check if the rock type is hard to add thirty to heat. If the rock type is exactly diamond, check if the bit state is boring to add one hundred to ore. If the coolant is empty, check if the bit state is not stopped to add forty to heat. If the rock type is not soft, check if the bit state is cooling to subtract twenty from heat. Return a list with ore extracted and heat level. Example: for [["boring", "soft", "active"], ["extracting", "hard", "active"], ["jammed", "hard", "empty"]], the output should be [70, 70].

title: Wind Turbine Yaw Controller
spec: Create a function `regulate(readings)` that takes a list of lists, each containing the turbine state, wind speed category, and power grid status. Maintain generated power and turbine stress, both starting at zero. If the turbine state is facing, check if the grid is connected to add fifty to power. If the turbine state is yawing, check if the wind speed is high to add five to stress. If the turbine state is braked, check if the grid is exactly offline to subtract ten from stress. If the wind speed is storm, check if the turbine state is not feathered to add one hundred to stress. If the turbine state is storm, check if the grid is connected to subtract twenty from stress. If the grid is disconnected, check if the turbine state is not braked to add thirty to stress. Return a list with generated power and stress. Example: for [["facing", "normal", "connected"], ["yawing", "high", "connected"], ["braked", "storm", "offline"]], the output should be [50, -5].

title: Archery Tournament Scorer
spec: Write `score(arrows)` to process a list of lists, where each entry records arrow placement on the target, wind conditions, and the archer category. Track total points and penalty count, both starting at zero. If the placement is bullseye, check if the wind is calm to add ten to points. If the placement is inner, check if the archer is guest to add eight to points. If the placement is outer, check if the wind is gusty to add five to points. If the placement is miss, check if the archer is not guest to add one to penalty. If the placement is exactly bounce, check if the wind is calm to add two to penalty. If the wind is storm, check if the placement is not miss to add twenty to points. Return a list with total points and the penalty count. Example: for [["bullseye", "calm", "pro"], ["inner", "breeze", "guest"], ["bounce", "calm", "guest"]], the output should be [18, 2].

title: Textile Loom Pattern Reader
spec: Write a function `weave(commands)` that processes a sequence of loom instructions to generate a fabric pattern. The machine tracks the shuttle position as either left or right, the hook status as raised or lowered, and the current thread color. If an instruction is halt, the weaving stops immediately and ignores remaining commands. If an instruction is pass, the shuttle moves to the opposite side and adds the current color to the output list, but only if the hook is raised. If the instruction is drop and the hook is raised, the hook becomes lowered. If the instruction is lift and the hook is lowered, the hook becomes raised. If the instruction is a new color, the color updates only if the shuttle is on the left. Return a list of the successfully woven color strings. For example, lifting the hook, changing color to red, passing, dropping the hook, passing, and lifting the hook again will output a list containing just red.

title: Seismograph Anomaly Detector
spec: Implement `detect(readings)` to filter and analyze geological vibrations. Each reading has a wave type, an amplitude number, and a sensor status. The function must ignore any reading where the sensor status is offline or calibrating. For active sensors, if the wave type is primary and the amplitude is exactly zero, it is discarded as a ghost signal. If the amplitude is exactly negative one, it is an equipment error and should be skipped. If the wave type is secondary and the immediately preceding valid wave was also secondary, increment a cluster counter. If the wave type is surface and the amplitude is greater than ten, flag it as a major event. Return a list containing the total valid readings, the cluster count, and the number of major events. An input of primary with amplitude five, followed by offline, followed by surface with amplitude twelve returns three numbers: two valid, zero clusters, and one major event.

title: Vintage Camera Exposure
spec: Create a function `calculate(conditions)` that determines the optimal shutter speed index for a mechanical camera. The input provides the lighting, the subject type, and the film speed. Start with a base index of ten. If the lighting is sunny, add two to the index; if it is overcast, subtract two; if it is dark, subtract five. If the subject is portrait and the lighting is not dark, subtract one to blur the background. If the subject is landscape and the lighting is sunny, add three. If the subject is macro, add one for depth of field unless the film speed is slow, in which case add two. If the lighting is overcast and the film speed is fast, ignore the subject modifiers completely. Return the final integer index. Given sunny, macro, and slow, the result is thirteen.

title: Mechanical Keyboard Switch Tester
spec: Write `evaluate(events)` to analyze the quality of a keyboard switch. The input is a list of sequential action strings from a testing rig. The switch state begins as idle. When a press action occurs, the state becomes descending. If a bottom action arrives, the state must currently be descending, otherwise record a sequence error. A release action changes the state to ascending, and a reset action returns it to idle. If a bounce action occurs while the state is ascending or descending, increment a bounce counter, but do not change the state. If a bounce happens while idle, record a severe fault. Return a list containing the number of successful complete cycles, total bounces, and total errors. For example, a sequence of press, bottom, release, bounce, reset yields one cycle, one bounce, and zero errors.

title: Telescope Mount Tracker
spec: Develop a function `align(signals)` to manage the movement states of an automated telescope. The telescope starts in a parked mode. When a wake signal is received, the mode changes to idle. A track signal changes an idle or slewing telescope into the tracking mode. A slew signal is only accepted if the current mode is idle or tracking. If a park signal arrives, the telescope must first be in idle mode to successfully transition back to parked; if it is tracking or slewing, the park signal is ignored and an error is tallied. Any track signal received while already parked is also tallied as an error. If the signal is abort, change the mode directly to parked and increment errors. Return a list with the final mode string and the total number of errors. An input of wake, slew, park, track results in a final mode of slewing and one error.

title: Antique Clock Escapement
spec: Write `simulate(ticks)` to model the internal mechanism of a pendulum clock. The clock tracks its active pallet, starting as none. Each tick provides a pendulum swing direction and a driving force string. If the direction is center, the pendulum is resting and the tick is ignored. If the direction is left and the pallet is none or exit, the active pallet becomes entry. If the direction is right and the pallet is entry, the active pallet becomes exit. However, if the force is weak when engaging the entry pallet, the clock stalls and all subsequent ticks are ignored. If the force is strong while the pallet is exit, increment a wear counter. Return the total successful swings and the wear counter as a list of two numbers. Given right, left with weak force, and right, the output is one successful swing and zero wear.

title: Radio Telescope Pulsar Filter
spec: Implement `filter(pulses)` to sift through space radio signals. Each pulse has a source category, a polarization type, and a width number. Start with empty lists for valid pulsars and anomalies. If the source is unknown, append it to the anomalies list. If the source is local or the source is interference, discard the pulse entirely. If the source is deep space and the polarization is circular, append the width to the valid pulsar list. If the source is deep space but the polarization is linear, check the width; if the width is exactly zero or greater than one hundred, append it to the anomalies list instead. If the polarization is unpolarized, discard the pulse regardless of the source. Return a list containing the valid pulsar list and the anomalies list. A local pulse and a deep space circular pulse of width ten returns a list with one valid list of ten and an empty anomaly list.

title: Fountain Pen Ink Flow
spec: Create `write(strokes)` to simulate drawing with a fountain pen. The pen starts with a pristine nib and an ink reservoir of twenty. Each stroke specifies a pressure level and an angle. If the reservoir is zero, ignore all strokes. If the pressure is heavy and the nib is pristine, the nib degrades to bent. If the pressure is heavy and the nib is already bent, it degrades to broken. A stroke with an acute angle consumes two units of ink if the nib is pristine, but three units if it is bent. A standard angle consumes one unit of ink, unless the nib is broken, which consumes none and fails to write. If the pressure is light, consume half a unit of ink less than normal. Return the final nib status and the total ink consumed. A heavy stroke at an acute angle followed by a standard stroke consumes four total units and leaves a bent nib.

title: Geiger Counter Radiation Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(particles)` to classify ionizing radiation events. Each particle has a classification, an energy level, and the current sensor shield status. If the shield is jammed, add ten to the hazard tally for any particle. If the shield status is closed, ignore any particle whose classification is alpha or beta. If the classification is alpha and the shield is open, increment the hazard tally by one. If the classification is beta and the shield is open, increment the hazard tally only if the energy level is exactly one hundred. If the classification is gamma, increment the hazard tally by five regardless of the shield status, unless the shield is testing, in which case add nothing. Return the final hazard tally. An alpha particle with an open shield and a gamma particle with a closed shield yields a tally of six.

title: Telegraph Relay Station
spec: Implement `route(messages)` to sort incoming telegraph transmissions. Each message has a priority string and a destination category. You must maintain three separate lists: urgent, normal, and dead letter. If the destination is unknown, always append the message content to the dead letter list. If the destination is testing, process it but do not append it to any list. If the priority is high and the destination is local, append it to the urgent list. If the priority is high and the destination is remote, also append it to the urgent list. If the priority is standard and the destination is local, append it to the normal list. If the priority is low and the destination is local, drop it entirely. If the priority is low and the destination is remote, send to dead letter. Return a list of the three lists in order of urgent, normal, and dead letter.

title: Glacier Movement Tracker
spec: Develop `analyze(scans)` to track ice sheet dynamics over time. Scans contain an ice zone, a thermal profile, and a fracture state. A zone can be accumulation, ablation, margin, or deep. If the fracture state is dormant, ignore the scan entirely. If the zone is accumulation and the thermal profile is warm, increment the melt counter. If the zone is deep and the thermal profile is warm, increment the melt counter by two. If the zone is ablation and the fracture state is active, check the thermal profile; if it is freezing, increment the slip counter, but if it is warm, increment the hazard counter. If the zone is margin, only increment the hazard counter if the fracture state is active and the thermal profile is not freezing. Return a list of the melt, slip, and hazard counters. An ablation zone that is active and freezing adds one to the slip counter.

title: Bicycle Gear Derailleur
spec: Create `shift(actions)` to simulate changing gears on a bicycle. The bike starts with the front chainring on small and the rear cassette on large. Actions can be front up, front down, rear up, or rear down. If the action is front up and the front is small, change it to large. If the action is front down and the front is large, change it to small. For the rear, an up action shifts large to medium, or medium to small. A down action shifts small to medium, or medium to large. If an action would cause the front to be large and the rear to be small simultaneously, ignore the action to prevent cross chaining. Return a list containing the final front and rear states. Front up, rear up, rear up starting from small and large ends in small and small because the first rear up succeeds but the second is blocked.

title: Darkroom Enlarger Timer
spec: Write `expose(parameters)` to calculate the base exposure time for a photographic print. The input lists a paper grade, a negative density, and a chemical temperature. Begin with a base time of fifteen seconds. If the paper grade is hard, add five seconds. If the paper grade is soft, subtract three seconds. If the negative density is thin, halve the current time. If the density is dense, double the current time. Finally, if the chemical temperature is cold, add ten seconds. If the temperature is hot, subtract five seconds. If the paper grade is normal and the density is normal and the temperature is optimal, make no changes. Return the final calculated time. A hard grade, dense negative, and hot temperature yields thirty five seconds.

title: Mechanical Cash Register
spec: Implement `transact(inputs)` to manage the state of an antique till. The register state begins as closed. Valid input commands are scan, total, pay, and void. If the command is scan and the state is closed, change the state to open and add one to the item count. If the command is scan and the state is open, add one to the item count. If the command is void and the state is open, subtract one from the item count, and if the item count reaches exactly zero, change the state to closed. If the command is total and the state is open, change the state to pending. If the command is pay and the state is pending, change the state to closed and reset the item count to zero. Return the final state and item count. Scanning twice, totaling, and paying leaves the register closed with zero items.

title: Gramophone Record Player
spec: Create `play(commands)` to simulate operating a vintage record player. The system tracks the motor state as off, thirty three, or forty five, and the stylus position as rest, edge, or center. If the command is switch speed, toggle the motor between thirty three and forty five, but only if the stylus is at the rest position. If the command is drop needle and the motor is off, record a scratch penalty. If drop needle occurs when the motor is not off, move the stylus to edge. If the command is play track and the stylus is edge, move it to center. If the command is auto return, the stylus must be at center to move back to rest, otherwise it does nothing. Return the final stylus position and the penalty count. A drop needle on an off motor yields a rest position and one penalty.

title: Astrolabe Star Finder
spec: Write a function `locate(settings)` to determine which constellations are visible through an astrolabe. The inputs provide the hemisphere, the current season, and the sky clarity. Start with an empty list of visible stars. If the clarity is perfectly clear and the season is spring, add Virgo. If the hemisphere is north and the season is winter, add Orion to the list. If the hemisphere is north and the season is summer, add Cygnus. If the hemisphere is south, add Crux regardless of the season, but if the season is autumn, also add Centaurus. If the sky clarity is cloudy, clear the entire list. If the sky clarity is hazy, remove Orion if it is in the list, as it sits too low on the horizon. Return the final list of constellations. A north winter sky that is hazy returns an empty list.

title: Steam Engine Governor
spec: Implement `govern(readings)` to adjust a steam intake valve based on operational metrics. The valve starts at a position of fifty. Each reading has a spin rate, a physical load, and a boiler pressure. If the spin rate is fast and the load is light, decrease the valve by ten. If the load is empty and the spin rate is fast, decrease the valve by twenty. If the spin rate is slow and the load is heavy, increase the valve by fifteen. If the boiler pressure is critical, immediately force the valve to zero, regardless of the spin rate or load. If the boiler pressure is low and the spin rate is optimal, increase the valve by five. Keep the valve position bounded between zero and one hundred. Return the final valve position. A fast spin with a light load and normal pressure leaves the valve at forty.

title: Semaphore Flag Signaler
spec: Develop `decode(positions)` to translate flag telegraph signals into words. The input is a list of poses, where each pose has a left arm position and a right arm position. If the left arm is low and the right arm is horizontal, output the letter A. If the left is low and the right is high, output B. If both arms are horizontal, output R. If the left is high and the right is low, output K. If the left is horizontal and the right is high, output J. If both arms are resting, output a space character. Any other combination of positions should output a question mark to indicate an unrecognized signal. Join the resulting characters and return the translated string. A sequence of low and horizontal, followed by resting, followed by high and low yields the string A K.

title: Waterwheel Millstone
spec: Create `grind(batches)` to simulate processing grain in a watermill. The mill has a water flow state of strong, weak, or blocked. Each batch specifies a grain type and a required texture. If the flow is blocked, no grain is processed, and the batch is skipped entirely. If the grain is wheat and the flow is strong, the output texture is fine. If the grain is wheat and the flow is weak, the output texture is coarse. If the grain is corn, it requires a strong flow to process; if the flow is weak, it outputs cracked instead of the required texture. If the grain is oats and the flow is strong, output rolled. If the grain is oats and the flow is weak, output steel cut. If the grain is barley, output pearl regardless of flow. Return a list of the actual output textures for all processed batches.

title: Hot Metal Typesetter
spec: Write `typeset(characters)` to assemble textual slugs for a printing press. The machine state tracks the active font, starting as roman. Valid font modifiers are italic, underline, and bold. If a character input is a font modifier string, change the active font to that style and output nothing. If the input is reset, change the active font back to roman. If the input is clear, discard the current line. If the input is indent, prepend four spaces. If the input is a regular word, append it to the current line. If the active font is italic, wrap the word in emphasis tags. If the active font is bold, wrap it in strong tags. If the active font is underline, wrap the word in underline tags. If the input is the word break, finalize the current line, add it to the page list, and start a new line. Return the page list.

title: Barometer Weather Forecaster
spec: Implement `predict(observations)` to generate weather outlooks based on atmospheric pressure. Each observation has a pressure trend and a wind direction. If the wind is calm, predict fog regardless of the trend. If the trend is falling and the wind is south, the forecast is severe storms. If the trend is falling and the wind is east, the forecast is heavy rain. If the trend is rising and the wind is north, the forecast is clear and cool. If the trend is rising and the wind is west, the forecast is fair and breezy. If the trend is steady, the forecast is no change, unless the wind is south, which predicts warmer temperatures. Return a list of forecast strings corresponding to the observations. A rising trend with a north wind yields clear and cool.

title: Avalanche Risk Assessor
spec: Develop `assess(layers)` to evaluate the stability of a snowpack. Each layer in the sequence (from top to bottom) has a crystal shape, a hardness string, and a wetness level. A weak layer is defined as having a faceted crystal shape and a soft hardness. A slab is defined as having a rounded crystal shape and a hard hardness. Iterate through the layers. If a weak layer is immediately followed by a slab layer, increment the critical danger count. If the shape is ice and the hardness is hard, increase critical danger by two. If a layer is wet and its shape is surface hoar, increment the slip hazard count. If a layer has a crust shape, regardless of hardness, decrease the critical danger count by one, but do not let it drop below zero. Return the critical danger and slip hazard counts.

title: Film Reel Splicer
spec: Create `splice(frames)` to process a movie reel for physical cuts. The sequence contains frame strings that can be picture, blank, scorch mark, title card, or splice tape. The system tracks the current scene state as ongoing or cut. If a blank frame is encountered and the scene is ongoing, increment the damage counter. If a blank frame appears while the state is cut, ignore it. If a scorch mark frame is encountered, increment the damage counter by five. If a title card frame is found, reset the repair counter to zero. If a splice tape is encountered, the scene state changes to cut. If a picture frame is encountered while the state is cut, the state changes back to ongoing, and the repair counter is incremented. If two splice tapes are encountered back to back, increment the fault counter. Return a list containing the damage, repair, and fault counters.

title: Diving Springboard Rater
spec: Write `score(phases)` to compute the technical execution of a springboard dive. The phases include approach, takeoff, flight, and entry. Each phase has a quality rating. Start with a base score of ten. If the approach quality is perfect, add two points. If the approach quality is unsteady, subtract two points. If the takeoff is balked, the score becomes exactly zero immediately. If the takeoff quality is low, subtract three points. If the flight quality is tucked, add one point. If the flight quality is straight, add two points. If the entry is ripped, add three points. If the entry quality is splashy, subtract four points. However, if the entry is splashy but the flight was straight, only subtract two points as a partial redemption. Return the final numeric score. An unsteady approach with a straight flight and splashy entry yields eight points.

title: Meteor Shower Observer
spec: Implement `catalog(sightings)` to identify the astronomical origin of shooting stars. Each sighting contains a velocity string, a trail length, and a primary color. If the velocity is fast and the trail is long, classify it as a Perseid, but only if the color is not red. If the velocity is slow and the color is yellow, classify it as a Geminid. If the velocity is medium and the trail is short, classify it as an Orionid. If the velocity is fast and the color is green, classify it as a Leonid, regardless of the trail length. Any sighting that does not match these criteria is classified as sporadic. Return a list of the classifications. A fast, long, white meteor is classified as a Perseid.

title: Insurance Claim Adjudicator
spec: Write a function `adjudicate(claims)` to process a list of medical claims. Each claim object has a policy status, a provider network, and a service category. A claim is approved if the policy status is active and the provider network is internal. If the policy status is active but the provider network is external, it is approved only if the service category is emergency; otherwise it is pending. If the policy status is suspended, the claim is pending unless the service category is preventive, in which case it is approved. If the policy status is terminated, the claim is denied. If the policy status is expired, the claim is denied regardless of other factors. Any claim with a service category of cosmetic is automatically denied. Return a list of final string decisions for each claim. For example, a claim with active status, internal network, and routine category returns approved.

title: Optical Prescription Lens Grinder
spec: Determine the manufacturing machine setting for lens orders using `grind(prescriptions)`. Each order specifies a material, a shape, and a coating. Use the standard setting if the material is glass and the shape is spherical. Use the advanced setting if the material is polycarbonate and the shape is aspheric. If the material is high index, use the delicate setting regardless of shape, unless the coating is anti reflective, which requires the premium setting, or the coating is tinted, which requires the custom setting. If the material is glass and the coating is scratch resistant, use the reinforced setting. If the material is plastic and the shape is cylindrical, use the basic setting. Return an array of the determined machine settings. For example, an order for glass material, spherical shape, and no coating returns standard.

title: Baggage Routing System
spec: Implement `route(bags)` to determine the sorting chute for airport luggage. Each bag has a flight type, a weight class, and a transfer status. Route to the primary chute if the flight type is domestic and the transfer status is final. Route to the secondary chute if the flight type is international and the transfer status is final. If the transfer status is transit, route to the expedited chute if the weight class is standard, but route to the manual chute if the weight class is oversized. Any bag with a flight type of charter goes to the special chute regardless of other properties. If the flight type is cargo and the transfer status is final, route to the warehouse chute. If the flight type is military, route to the secure chute. Return an array of chute assignments. For example, a domestic flight, standard weight, and final transfer routes to primary.

title: University Prerequisite Checker
spec: Assess whether students can enroll in a capstone seminar with `evaluate(students)`. Each student has a major, an academic standing, a disciplinary record, and a thesis status. A student is eligible if their major is engineering, their academic standing is senior, and their disciplinary record is clear. If their major is mathematics, they are eligible if their academic standing is senior and their thesis status is submitted. If their academic standing is junior, they are only eligible if their thesis status is approved and their disciplinary record is clear. Any student whose disciplinary record is probation is ineligible. If the major is physics and the academic standing is sophomore, they are ineligible. If the thesis status is rejected, they are ineligible. Return a list of boolean eligibility results. For example, an engineering senior with a clear record and no thesis returns true.

title: Waste Management Sorting
spec: Categorize items arriving at a recycling facility via `sort(items)`. Each item has a base material, a contamination level, and a physical form. Route to the paper line if the base material is cardboard and the contamination level is low. Route to the plastic line if the base material is polymer and the physical form is rigid. If the contamination level is high, route to the landfill unless the base material is metal, in which case route to the wash station. Route to the glass line if the base material is silica and the contamination level is low. If the base material is textile and the contamination level is low, route to the donate bin. If the base material is polymer and the physical form is flexible, route to the baler. Return a list of destination lines. For example, polymer base, low contamination, and rigid form goes to plastic line.

title: Blood Bank Matching
spec: Filter a list of blood donations for a patient requiring a specific transfusion using `match(donors)`. Each donation has a blood group, an rhesus factor, and an antibody screen result. Accept the donation if the blood group is universal and the antibody screen result is negative. If the blood group is matched, accept it only if the rhesus factor is negative and the antibody screen result is negative. Reject any donation where the antibody screen result is positive or the blood group is incompatible. If the blood group is matched and the rhesus factor is positive, flag it for secondary testing. If the blood group is universal but the rhesus factor is positive, flag for secondary testing. If the blood group is unknown, route to quarantine. Return a list of string outcomes. For example, universal group, negative rhesus, and negative antibodies returns accepted.

title: Art Gallery Lighting Controller
spec: Determine the optimal lighting profile for museum displays with `illuminate(artworks)`. Each artwork has a creative medium, a conservation status, and a framing type. Apply the dim profile if the creative medium is watercolor and the conservation status is fragile. Apply the bright profile if the creative medium is sculpture and the framing type is exposed. Apply the standard profile if the creative medium is oil painting, unless the conservation status is restored, which requires the soft profile. If the framing type is glass, apply the glare reduction profile regardless of medium, unless it is a fragile watercolor, which always takes the dim profile. If the creative medium is tapestry, apply the ambient profile. If the creative medium is acrylic and the framing type is exposed, apply the bright profile. Return an array of lighting profiles. For example, a fragile watercolor under glass requires dim.

title: Veterinary Clinic Appointment Scheduler
spec: Prioritize arriving animal patients using `schedule(appointments)`. Each patient has a species category, a visit reason, and a fasting status. Assign immediate priority if the visit reason is trauma or the visit reason is breathing difficulty. Assign high priority if the species category is exotic and the visit reason is illness. If the visit reason is surgery, assign high priority only if the fasting status is confirmed; otherwise assign delayed priority. Assign routine priority if the visit reason is vaccination and the species category is domestic. If the visit reason is dental and the species category is domestic, assign routine priority. If the species category is exotic and the visit reason is boarding, assign delayed priority. Return an array of priority assignments. For example, an exotic animal arriving for trauma gets immediate priority.

title: Building Security Access System
spec: Evaluate employee badge swipes at various building zones with `authorize(requests)`. Each request has an employee role, a target zone, and a clearance level. Grant access if the target zone is lobby and the clearance level is basic. Grant access if the target zone is server room, the employee role is administrator, and the clearance level is elevated. Deny access if the target zone is executive suite and the clearance level is basic. If the target zone is laboratory, grant access only if the employee role is researcher or the clearance level is maximum. If the target zone is cafeteria and the clearance level is basic, grant access. If the target zone is parking garage and the clearance level is basic, grant access. If the employee role is maintenance and the target zone is server room, deny access. Return a list of granted or denied strings. For example, a researcher with basic clearance accessing the laboratory receives granted.

title: Logistics Freight Router
spec: Determine the transport method for outgoing freight via `dispatch(shipments)`. Each shipment has a temperature requirement, a delivery speed, and a hazard classification. Use refrigerated air if the temperature requirement is frozen and the delivery speed is overnight. Use refrigerated truck if the temperature requirement is frozen and the delivery speed is standard. Use secure air if the hazard classification is radioactive and the delivery speed is overnight. If the hazard classification is flammable, use ground transport regardless of delivery speed, unless the temperature requirement is chilled, which requires specialized ground. If the hazard classification is fragile and the delivery speed is overnight, use padded air. If the hazard classification is fragile and the delivery speed is standard, use padded ground. Return a list of transport methods. For example, standard speed, frozen, and no hazard returns refrigerated truck.

title: Real Estate Property Appraiser
spec: Classify the market tier of residential homes using `appraise(properties)`. Each property has a zoning type, a structural condition, and a neighborhood rating. Classify as premium if the zoning type is residential, the structural condition is pristine, and the neighborhood rating is excellent. Classify as standard if the zoning type is residential and the structural condition is good. If the structural condition is dilapidated, classify as teardown unless the zoning type is commercial, in which case classify as redevelopment. If the neighborhood rating is poor and the structural condition is good, classify as starter. If the zoning type is industrial and the structural condition is pristine, classify as commercial premium. If the zoning type is agricultural, classify as farmland. Return a list of market tiers. For example, residential, pristine, excellent returns premium.

title: E-commerce Fraud Detector
spec: Flag online purchases for potential fraud review with `screen(transactions)`. Each transaction has a payment method, a shipping destination, and an account age. Flag as critical if the payment method is wire transfer and the shipping destination is international. Flag as high risk if the payment method is credit card, the shipping destination is international, and the account age is new. Approve automatically if the payment method is digital wallet and the account age is veteran. If the payment method is gift card and the account age is new, flag as moderate risk. If the payment method is cryptocurrency, flag for manual review. If the payment method is bank transfer and the shipping destination is domestic, approve automatically. If the payment method is credit card and the account age is veteran, approve automatically. Return a list of string risk assessments. For example, a veteran account using a digital wallet returns approve automatically.

title: Factory Quality Assurance
spec: Evaluate manufactured parts off an assembly line using `inspect(components)`. Each component has a surface finish, a dimensional tolerance, and a material temper. Accept the part if the surface finish is smooth, the dimensional tolerance is exact, and the material temper is hardened. Rework the part if the dimensional tolerance is wide and the material temper is hardened. Scrap the part if the material temper is soft and the dimensional tolerance is wide. If the surface finish is rough, scrap it unless the dimensional tolerance is exact, in which case route it for polishing. If the material temper is brittle and the dimensional tolerance is exact, route for stress test. If the material temper is brittle and the dimensional tolerance is wide, scrap it outright. Return an array of inspection outcomes. For example, smooth finish, exact tolerance, and hardened temper returns accept.

title: Municipal Tax Assessor
spec: Determine the tax bracket for city land parcels via `assess(parcels)`. Each parcel has a primary use, a developmental stage, and an ownership type. Assign the exempt bracket if the ownership type is municipal or the primary use is religious. Assign the commercial bracket if the primary use is retail and the developmental stage is completed. If the developmental stage is vacant, assign the speculative bracket unless the primary use is agricultural, which gets the rural bracket. Assign the residential bracket if the primary use is housing and the ownership type is private. If the primary use is industrial and the developmental stage is completed, assign the heavy commercial bracket. If the primary use is educational, assign the exempt bracket. Return a list of tax brackets. For example, a completed retail parcel owned privately gets the commercial bracket.

title: Software Bug Triager
spec: Categorize incoming software bug reports to development teams using `triage(issues)`. Each issue has a severity level, a reproducible status, and a system component. Assign to the hotfix team if the severity level is critical and the reproducible status is consistent. Assign to the backend team if the system component is database and the severity level is high. If the reproducible status is intermittent, assign to the investigation team unless the severity level is low, which goes to the backlog.
